persona_summary: I am a cryptographer who participated in the NIST PQC standardization rounds and signed onto the IETF LAMPS composite-sigs adoption call — I am NOT anti-PQ on principle. I support eventual PQ-hybrid signature adoption. But I am skeptical of treating the `ml-dsa` Rust crate as production-ready before independent audit and formal verification, and I am skeptical of the framing that 'classical Ed25519 is our audited security floor' suffices as a safety story for v1-beta DEFAULT deployment of an unaudited PQ implementation. My concern is not whether to ship PQ-hybrid eventually but whether the proposed Position-B blog post correctly characterizes the safety properties of what Benten has actually built, in the presence of side-channel literature published 2025-2026 demonstrating practical private-key recovery attacks against unmasked ML-DSA implementations — including a documented timing side-channel in the EXACT `ml-dsa` Rust crate Benten depends on (GHSA-hcp2-x6j4-29j7, disclosed 2026-01-09, ~4 months before this lens dispatch).
evidence_base_verified: RustCrypto `ml-dsa` advisory GHSA-hcp2-x6j4-29j7 — timing side-channel in Decompose's UDIV/SDIV could leak private key material; disclosed 2026-01-09; fixed only in 0.1.0-rc.3 by replacing division with constant-time Barrett reduction. Benten's `Cargo.lock` pins `ml-dsa 0.1.0` (post-fix per advisory wording, but the bug shipped to production for months and the same class likely lurks elsewhere — see below).

IACR eprint 2025/582 ('Release the Power of Rejected Signatures: An Efficient Side-Channel Attack on the ML-DSA Cryptosystem'). Practical key-recovery exploiting BOTH valid and rejected signature trials.

IACR eprint 2026/056 ('Rejection Matters: Efficient Non-Profiling Side-Channel Attack on ML-DSA via Exploiting Public Templates'). Published January 2026 — same month as the RustCrypto patch — demonstrating first SCA jointly leveraging rejected + final trial leakage WITHOUT clone devices. Non-profiling = weaker adversary assumption = practical threat.

NIST 6th PQC Standardization Conference 2025 talk: 'Recent Contributions to the Physical Security of ML-DSA'. Quote: 'ML-DSA must be almost entirely protected against side-channel attacks, in contrast to ECDSA which requires mitigations only for several of its operations.' (Source: csrc.nist.gov)

Project Eleven 'The State of Post-Quantum Cryptography in Rust: The Belt is Vacant' (2025): explicit finding that NO RustCrypto post-quantum package has undergone independent audit; the `ml-dsa` README carries 'USE AT YOUR OWN RISK' warning verbatim. Same crate Benten depends on.

Additional CVE GHSA-5x2r-hc65-25f9 — ML-DSA verification accepts signatures with repeated hint indices (medium severity, RustCrypto `ml-dsa`). Demonstrates the crate has had MULTIPLE correctness/security issues since publication.

libcrux-ml-dsa (cryspen) — alternative formally-verified-with-hax+F* Rust ML-DSA crate; field arithmetic + NTT + serialization mechanized. NOT what Benten uses. November 2025 bug: v0.0.3 produced different keys/sigs on ARM Linux vs Apple Silicon for same seed — even formally-verified PQ implementations have shipped reproducibility bugs.

Agent-2 §A.1: LAMPS composite-sigs draft-19 in RFC Editor Queue; OIDs early-allocated 2025-10-20. Security analysis from LAMPS WG ONLY — no IACR peer-reviewed paper on the COMPOSITE construction itself. Compare X-Wing KEM combiner: full IACR Communications in Cryptology 2024 paper (Barbosa/Connolly/Duits/Schwabe/Schmieg/Stebila). Composite-sig combiner does NOT have equivalent depth of analysis.

Agent-3 §C: every shipped P2P/messaging system (iroh, Signal PQXDH, Apple PQ3, Cloudflare, MLS-default 7-of-9 ciphersuites, Veilid, Tor) keeps signatures CLASSICAL even when shipping PQ-hybrid KEM. iroh explicit quote: 'no industry consensus yet which one to use.' The tribe of cryptographers I belong to is deferring for substantive reasons that the blog draft does not adequately engage.

per_path.rationale: Supportive comments on container-form multicodec PRs are low-risk + cryptographically neutral. The PRs are about codepoint shape (per-algorithm vs container), not about whether to ship PQ-hybrid sigs today. Endorsing container-form even strengthens my position: it makes it CHEAPER to swap out unaudited ML-DSA-65 for libcrux-ml-dsa or a future audited implementation without churning the codepoint. PURSUE. (Caveat: the comments should NOT inadvertently legitimize Benten's deployment choice as a proof-point — keep them narrow on the codepoint-shape question.)

per_path.path: F3 — JOSE WG draft contribution to draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-01
per_path.rationale: The JOSE draft was just WG-adopted (Feb 2026); v01 is early enough that an adopter use-case meaningfully shapes the spec. Engaging with the standards process is the RIGHT response to my concerns: pushing for explicit guidance on (a) which audited implementations exist, (b) side-channel-protection requirements text, (c) algorithm-selection guidance for retrospective-forgery-sensitive deployments. PURSUE — but the contribution should include a 'deployment considerations' section that surfaces ML-DSA's exceptional side-channel sensitivity (NIST 2025 conference quote). Pushing JOSE WG to bake mitigation guidance into the spec is the right place to do this work.

per_path.path: F4 — LAMPS WG mailing list engagement (adopter perspective)
per_path.rationale: Mixed. POSITIVE: LAMPS WG genuinely benefits from real adopter feedback — and reporting Benten's deployment honestly (including the 'we are SHIPPING the unaudited Rust crate and accepting that risk for v1-beta with the audit gating v1-GM' framing) is useful WG signal. NEGATIVE: positioning Benten as a published adopter REINFORCES the perception that the composite-sig construction has production-deployment validation when in fact (i) the construction has only WG-level analysis (not IACR-peer-reviewed like X-Wing), (ii) the Rust implementation is unaudited, (iii) ALL other surveyed shipped P2P systems deferred precisely because of (i)+(ii). If the LAMPS engagement is framed as 'here is feedback from an adopter who shipped despite our reservations,' fine. If framed as 'here is validation that the construction is production-ready,' NOT fine. The framing decision is the gate. Defer until post-v1-beta-tag (as Section 6 already proposes) AND make the framing constraint explicit in the brief.

per_path.path: F5 — Blog post on benten.computer/blog (load-bearing primary signal)
per_path.rationale: This is where my persona has the SHARPEST objection — strong recommendation to revise the framing before publication, NOT to abandon the blog. As currently drafted (Section 2 + Section 3 outline), the post overstates the safety story in three load-bearing ways that I would call out publicly if I read it: (1) The 'classical Ed25519 audited security floor' claim is true for FORGERY resistance but DOES NOT defend against a side-channel attack on the `ml-dsa` Rust implementation that LEAKS THE ML-DSA PRIVATE KEY MATERIAL. Once the ML-DSA private key is leaked via SCA on a signing device, an attacker can produce signatures whose ML-DSA half verifies (because they have the key) and pair them with the same device's leaked-or-still-valid Ed25519 key — the hybrid combiner gives zero protection against this. The 'shippable with classical floor' argument addresses CRYPTANALYTIC compromise of ML-DSA (where the algorithm itself breaks), NOT IMPLEMENTATION compromise (where keys leak via timing/power/EM). The Lens 10 (audit-discipline) brief surfaces this distinction; my persona reinforces it from the SCA-literature side. (2) Honesty caveat #3 ('ml-dsa Rust crate is not yet independently audited. Audit is committed v1-beta deliverable + gates v1-GM') is structurally inadequate. The crate has shipped at least TWO security advisories (GHSA-hcp2-x6j4-29j7 timing leak + GHSA-5x2r-hc65-25f9 verification flaw) in its v0.x lifetime; one was disclosed FOUR MONTHS before this lens dispatch and could leak private keys. 'Audit gates v1-GM' is correct discipline, but the caveat should also disclose that (a) the specific crate has had public security issues, (b) ML-DSA implementations are KNOWN per NIST 2025 conference materials to require near-total SCA hardening, (c) Benten's own deployment is not running on attested HSMs / dedicated signing servers (it's running in user-process on commodity laptops / phones / browsers under the three-deployment-shapes commitment), where timing SCA is MORE practical than in HSM-style deployments. (3) The 'hybrid sigs less analysis than hybrid KEMs (X-Wing has IACR CiC 2024 paper; LAMPS composite-sigs has WG analysis only)' point — which is in this brief's own persona description AND in Agent-2 §A.1 — is NOT carried into the public blog framing at all. The blog implies (Section 2.1 'Strip-resistance of LAMPS construction' paragraph) that the LAMPS combiner is on equivalent analytical footing to X-Wing. It is NOT. PURSUE the blog WITH the framing-revisions enumerated in `specific_blog_text_changes_requested` below; otherwise DO NOT PUBLISH. If the blog ships as drafted, I (or my real-world equivalent) would publicly characterize it as overstating the safety story — that is a reputation cost Benten should not absorb when the revisions are cheap.

per_path.path: F6 — Open-source did:jwk hybrid extension library (standalone)
per_path.rationale: This is the BEST single move from my perspective. 'We shipped the code, here it is to inspect' is the asymmetric trust-builder Benten needs, and it converts the unaudited-substrate concern from 'Benten is hiding behind a deployment' to 'Benten is offering its construction for community scrutiny' — exactly the right cryptographic discipline. PURSUE strongly. Two refinements: (a) ship test vectors + known-answer-tests against the LAMPS draft-19 spec — this lets reviewers verify Benten's combiner matches the spec construction byte-for-byte (closes the 'are you sure your composite implementation is correct' question). (b) make the dependency on RustCrypto `ml-dsa` explicit + document the side-channel-protection posture (does Benten's signing path run on the same machine as untrusted code? if so, document timing-SCA as a residual risk and the mitigation plan). The library is the place where the persona's concerns become CONSTRUCTIVE: it lets the wider crypto community help find issues BEFORE v1-beta scales.

per_path.path: F7 — W3C CCG community engagement (did:key issues #70/#74)
per_path.rationale: Cryptographically neutral; the discussion is about codepoint placement in did:key, not about whether to ship PQ-hybrid. PURSUE. (The substantive cryptographic objections — on side-channel + audit + combiner-analysis-depth — do not engage the W3C CCG conversation; that conversation is about DID method design.) Light-touch supporting move.

per_path.path: F10 — Cross-system coordination outreach (iroh / Signal / MLS / Veilid)
per_path.rationale: Critical. iroh-first is correct. From my persona: the iroh team's 2026-05-19 blog post explicitly defers PQ-signatures pending 'industry consensus,' which is a polite way of saying what the SCA literature backs up: the Rust ML-DSA substrate is not yet ready for deployment-as-default at iroh's scale or threat model. Benten reaching out to iroh BEFORE the public blog gives iroh a chance to say 'yes we see your asymmetry argument; we agree it applies to content-addressed persistent artifacts but not to our transport-key threat model' — that is a coalition-shaped outcome, NOT 'iroh endorses Benten's PQ-hybrid sig deployment.' PURSUE. Important framing: the outreach should NOT ask iroh to validate the unaudited-substrate decision; it should ask iroh to validate the THREAT MODEL ASYMMETRY argument. Those are very different requests + the former would (rightly) get a polite no. Also support Signal / MLS WG outreach: not for endorsement, but for genuine engagement with their per-message-sig reasoning (Lens 8 surfaces this) — that engagement might surface a third-way argument neither side has fully articulated.

cross_path_synthesis.summary: From the PQ-skeptic-cryptographer persona, 6 of 7 PURSUE-set paths are net-positive AS LONG AS the blog framing (F5) is revised. The blog is the load-bearing artifact — if it overstates the safety story, the other 6 paths' supporting moves amplify a flawed signal across multiple audiences. If the blog is revised per the changes enumerated below, the entire 7-path slate is sound and I (or my real-world equivalent) would not publicly push back against it. Important: NONE of my objections argue against shipping PQ-hybrid sigs in Benten — they argue against the BLOG OVERSTATING the safety properties of an unaudited PQ implementation deployed in user-process on commodity hardware. The substantive deployment decision is legitimately Ben's call given the stated v1-beta-to-v1-GM audit-gating discipline (CLAUDE.md NF-2 / C-GM-AUDIT); my concern is exclusively about the PUBLIC-FACING framing. The Section 4 dispatch slate's own choice to include this lens at HIGH priority alongside L10 (audit-discipline) acknowledges that the framing-vs-substrate distinction is the load-bearing surface.
cross_path_synthesis.convergence_with_other_lenses: Aligns with L10 (audit-discipline) on the implementation-vs-algorithmic-weakness distinction; aligns with L9 (LAMPS-WG-participant) on the 'pre-RFC + early-allocation' caveat strengthening; aligns with L12 (combiner-soundness) on 'strip-resistant against downgrade, NOT against simultaneous compromise' language tightening; aligns with L15 (threat-model-boundaries) by raising the question 'why didn't Filecoin/Arweave/Sigstore make this choice given the same threat model?' — my persona's answer is partly because the SUBSTRATE wasn't ready, which adds a non-arrogance reason to the threat-model comparison.
cross_path_synthesis.downgrade_recommendation: If Ben + orchestrator weigh L2 + L10 + L15 returns AND decide the framing revisions are not feasible OR not desired, DOWNGRADE F5 from Position B ('why content-addressed long-term-persistence systems should consider this') to Position A ('why Benten chose this'). Position A is honest, defensible, and does NOT require the safety-story revisions to be airtight (because it doesn't make an ecosystem-prescriptive claim that invites the SCA-literature pushback). The F6 library + F2 + F7 + F3 + F4 + F10 supporting paths all remain sound under Position A. This downgrade path is exactly what Section 5 'Failure mode E' anticipates; from my persona, the conditions to trigger it are not yet met IF the F5 framing revisions land — but the orchestrator should treat L2's verdict as conditional on those revisions.
cross_path_synthesis.does_not_object_to_any_path_outright: No PURSUE-set path is VETOed. The substrate concern (unaudited ML-DSA Rust crate + ongoing SCA literature + LAMPS-construction analysis-depth gap) is a FRAMING concern at F5 and a sharpened-caveat concern at F4 — not a 'do not pursue any of these' concern.

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.current_implied_text: 'Strip-resistance of LAMPS construction: forging requires breaking BOTH halves.'
specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_replacement: Replace with: 'Strip-resistance of the LAMPS construction (against downgrade-style attacks): forging a valid composite signature without compromising both signing keys requires breaking BOTH the ML-DSA-65 half AND the Ed25519 half cryptanalytically. NOTE: this property defends against ALGORITHMIC compromise of either half (e.g. a future CRQC breaking Ed25519, or an unforeseen lattice-cryptanalysis advance against ML-DSA-65). It does NOT defend against IMPLEMENTATION compromise of either half — specifically, if a side-channel attack against the `ml-dsa` implementation on the signing device leaks the ML-DSA-65 private key, an attacker holding the leaked key can generate composite signatures whose ML-DSA half verifies correctly. The hybrid combiner is an algorithmic-failure hedge, not an implementation-failure hedge. See honesty caveats #3 + the new caveat #6 for the implementation-side mitigations.'

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.current_text: 'ml-dsa Rust crate is not yet independently audited. Audit is committed v1-beta deliverable + gates v1-GM (NF-2 / C-GM-AUDIT). Classical Ed25519 half is our audited security floor.'
specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_replacement: 'The `ml-dsa` Rust crate (RustCrypto, version 0.1.0 — the one Benten ships in v1-beta) is not yet independently audited; the crate's own README carries a USE AT YOUR OWN RISK warning. Two security advisories have been published against this crate during its 0.x lifetime: GHSA-hcp2-x6j4-29j7 (timing side-channel in Decompose that could leak ML-DSA private key material, disclosed 2026-01-09, fixed in 0.1.0-rc.3) and GHSA-5x2r-hc65-25f9 (verification accepts signatures with repeated hint indices, medium severity). Both are now patched, and Benten ships the post-fix version. Independent algorithmic audit of the pinned `ml-dsa` + `ml-kem` versions is a committed v1-beta deliverable that GATES the v1-GM tag (NF-2 / C-GM-AUDIT exit criterion). Until that audit lands: (a) the classical Ed25519 half remains the cryptanalytic-forgery-resistance floor — but is NOT a defense against side-channel implementation attacks that leak the ML-DSA private key; (b) ML-DSA implementations are KNOWN per NIST 6th PQC Standardization Conference (2025) materials to require near-total side-channel hardening (in contrast to ECDSA which requires mitigations only for specific operations); (c) recent academic results (IACR eprint 2025/582; 2026/056) demonstrate practical key-recovery side-channel attacks against unmasked ML-DSA implementations using leakage from both valid and rejected signature trials. Benten\'s deployment runs the signing code in user-process on commodity hardware (laptops / phones / browsers under the three-deployment-shapes commitment), which is the threat regime where these attacks are most practical. Benten\'s mitigation posture is: track upstream RustCrypto + libcrux-ml-dsa (formally-verified-with-hax+F* alternative) + commission independent audit before v1-GM. If you are deploying Benten in a threat regime where local attackers can measure signing timing — e.g. shared-tenancy server hosting signing keys, or a browser tab adjacent to attacker JavaScript — wait for v1-GM.'

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_new_text: 'The LAMPS composite-sigs construction (`Prefix || Label || len(ctx) || ctx || PH(M)` with fixed prefix `CompositeAlgorithmSignatures2025`, signing both ML-DSA-65 and Ed25519 against the same M\') has received analysis from the IETF LAMPS Working Group. It does NOT yet have an independent peer-reviewed cryptographic paper of the depth of the X-Wing KEM combiner (Barbosa/Connolly/Duits/Schwabe/Schmieg/Stebila, IACR Communications in Cryptology 2024-1-21). The construction is sound on its face — the algorithm-specific Label folded into M\' provides strong commitment, and the fixed prefix provides domain separation — but the depth of formal analysis is asymmetric between hybrid-KEM (deep) and hybrid-signature (WG-level). We are SHIPPING the LAMPS construction as drafted in draft-19; we recommend others evaluating composite-sigs deployment factor in this asymmetry vs the hybrid-KEM side.'

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.section: Section 4 (blog) 'Class of systems this argument applies to'
specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_addition: Add a paragraph explicitly noting that the argument applies to systems whose deployment substrate can support the side-channel mitigations ML-DSA requires. For systems shipping in environments where signing keys live in attested hardware modules (HSM-backed CA signing, secure-element-backed mobile keystore) the SCA threat is bounded by the HSM/secure-element implementation; for systems shipping in user-process on commodity hardware (which is Benten's three-shape posture per CLAUDE.md baked-in #17) the SCA threat is in scope and the implementation-audit gating is load-bearing.

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_emphasis_change: Lead this section with the implementation-vs-algorithm distinction (the substance of revised caveat #3 + new caveat #6). The current draft outline buries the strongest objection at honesty-caveat-position-#3-of-5; my persona reads this as 'they know but they hid it.' Surface it as the FIRST + LONGEST honesty caveat instead.

specific_blog_text_changes_requested.requested_addition: Add explicit items: (a) we'd like to see a formal-verification-tracking effort for at least one production ML-DSA Rust implementation (libcrux-ml-dsa shows the path); (b) we'd like to see the LAMPS composite-sig combiner receive an independent peer-reviewed analysis at X-Wing depth; (c) we'd like to see published guidance on side-channel-mitigation expectations for ML-DSA in user-process deployment contexts.

objection_1.statement: Benten ships the post-fix `ml-dsa 0.1.0` per Cargo.lock — the GHSA timing leak is fixed, so why is it relevant to the blog framing?
objection_1.response: Two reasons. First, the bug class (variable-time hardware division ops on secret-derived operands) is the SAME class repeatedly surfaced across the ML-DSA SCA literature (IACR 2025/582 + 2026/056 + the broader CRYSTALS-Dilithium key-recovery literature). A single fix to one Decompose function does not give confidence that the rest of the crate is free of the same bug class — only an independent audit + formal-verification effort + adversarial SCA evaluation provides that confidence. Second, the v1-beta-to-v1-GM window is intentionally an audit gap; the blog is honestly characterizing what's deployed during that window, and 'we shipped a crate that had a private-key-leaking timing bug fixed four months before publication' is exactly the kind of fact that a transparent honesty caveat should disclose. Hiding it imports reputation risk at the moment the next SCA paper drops (and there WILL be a next one — the literature is active).

objection_2.statement: The blog already has the v1-beta vs v1-GM audit-gate framing; isn't that enough?
objection_2.response: No. The current draft frames the gate as 'audit is committed; you can trust us to land it before v1-GM.' That framing is fine for v1-GM. But the BLOG publishes during v1-beta — i.e., during the gap. The blog needs to characterize the v1-beta substrate's actual safety story honestly, not point at v1-GM and say 'wait for that.' Anyone reading the blog when v1-beta ships will (rightly) ask 'so what are you running today?' and the answer needs to be the truthful one: 'we ship an unaudited PQ implementation, paired with an audited classical implementation, with the hybrid combiner protecting against algorithmic failure of either half — but if implementation-level SCA against ML-DSA gets your private key, the combiner does not help.' That is a defensible thing to ship; pretending it isn't true is not.

objection_3.statement: If we add all these caveats, the blog reads like a self-criticism and undermines the entire 'stake out PQ-hybrid sigs for content-addressed systems' message.
objection_3.response: Disagree from my persona. The cryptographer audience this blog targets (LAMPS WG / NIST PQC participants / iroh-team / Signal-team / academic SCA researchers) READS the careful caveats as the marker of competence — handwaving the implementation-vs-algorithm distinction is what marks a blog as not-to-be-trusted. The audiences who would respond to a less-careful framing (general developers / HN front page) are also the audiences whose endorsement does not help with the actual standards-body engagement Benten wants. The blog reads BETTER with the caveats foregrounded, not worse. Cite analog: Signal's PQXDH whitepaper is upfront about exactly what its PQ properties protect against and what they don't; that whitepaper is widely respected precisely because of that posture.

objection_4.statement: Aren't you holding Benten to a standard that no shipped P2P system meets? Most of them are silent about side-channels and just ship.
objection_4.response: Most shipped P2P systems also do NOT ship PQ-hybrid signatures (Agent-3's central finding). The systems that DO ship PQ — Cloudflare TLS, Signal PQXDH, Apple PQ3, iroh PQ-KEM — ship PQ-KEM where the relevant SCA threat is different (and where industrial implementations live in HSMs or secure elements). Benten is making a more aggressive deployment choice (PQ on the SIG side, in user-process, on commodity hardware), so the disclosure standard should be correspondingly more careful. The 'no one else discloses' argument doesn't apply when 'no one else is shipping the thing you're shipping.'

objection_5.statement: Couldn't the side-channel concern be relegated to the F6 library README + closed at the blog with a one-line pointer?
objection_5.response: No — for two reasons. (1) Most blog readers will NOT click through to the library README, so the load-bearing safety claim lives in the blog text wherever it actually appears. (2) The current blog's load-bearing 'classical floor' framing IS the implicit safety claim, and that claim is wrong about the SCA threat model. You can't pointer-out a wrong claim; you have to fix the claim. The library README should ALSO carry the SCA-mitigation posture (this is implementation-doc-coupling per pim-1 §3.5b), but the blog's framing is the primary problem.

what_would_change_my_verdict: If F5 is revised per the specific text changes above, my F5 verdict moves from −1 to + (full support).

If F5 is downgraded to Position A ('why Benten chose this') rather than Position B ('why content-addressed systems should consider this'), my F5 verdict moves to + without requiring the text changes (Position A doesn't make the ecosystem-prescriptive claim that invites the SCA-literature pushback).

If F4 (LAMPS adopter report) is framed as 'feedback from a shipping-despite-reservations adopter' rather than 'validation that the construction is production-ready,' my F4 verdict moves from NEUTRAL to +.

If Benten commits to tracking libcrux-ml-dsa (cryspen, formally-verified-with-hax+F*) as a future swap target + makes the swap reversibility a stated v1-beta property — i.e. 'we can flip implementations without breaking the wire format' — that further strengthens every path. The crypto-agility framing already implies this; making it explicit in F5 + F6 would be a confidence-builder.

Recommend the orchestrator NOT publish the blog until L2 + L10 + L15 returns have been synthesized AND the F5 text changes (or Position-A downgrade) have been ratified by Ben — this matches the Section 5 'failure mode E' gate.

Cite-grep-verify discipline applied throughout: all IACR eprint numbers, GHSA IDs, version numbers (`ml-dsa 0.1.0`), OIDs (`1.3.6.1.5.5.7.6.48`), and the LAMPS-construction string ('CompositeAlgorithmSignatures2025') verified against the named source documents + Cargo.lock + live web-search hits where applicable.
